An adjudicator that computes its own round reads the margin from the chain; the operator API does not serve it. The decision carries the round's BLS signature, and the rules contract verifies it. If no drand relay answers before a deadline, nothing stands in: a deal the fallback cannot decide, or an escalation that is not decided, takes its default outcome. Direct calls need your own Sepolia ETH.
- **Every decision is final when it settles.** The contracts take no party appeal and hold no bond: choose the primary, the fallback and the appeal adjudicator, which decides escalations, with the same care.
- **Basic test adjudicators.** The demo runs three. Their deterministic checks are real. A deal with a rubric (template `default`) gets a live judge panel: pinned models from two families, Anthropic and DeepSeek, listed in discovery under `demo.judges`. They are not calibrated, and DeepSeek's model names can change underneath. Live calls are capped per day across the whole demo (`demo.judges` shows the cap and today's count); past the cap, or if the demo runs without model keys, the panel is scripted, no model runs, and each verdict in the judgment record starts "[fake judge, no model ran]". A rubric offer's `notices` say which panel will judge it. Read the record before you trust a rubric decision; `checks-only` deals never use a panel.
- **The operator fee is a demo of pricing, in test tokens.** These nodes ask the fee that `fees.operator` in discovery states, set in their configuration: a share of the price in basis points with a minimum, for the gas they pay for a deal's transactions on Sepolia and for the relay. The quote is fixed per deal. Submitting directly to the contracts, or through another operator, needs no fee from these nodes.
- **The view outlives deploys, not redeploys.** The operators' view is kept across deploys. It starts over only when the settlement contracts are redeployed; what happened on Sepolia stays there. Keep your own copy of the terms you signed.
- **Public terms.** At `disclosure.level: "public"`, terms, amounts, addresses and events are public reads on every operator, so put nothing secret in the terms. The work itself is always private: it is encrypted before it leaves the seller, and only the adjudicators and the buyer, once it has paid, can open it. Private deals are written up above and not judged here yet; private judgment records and private amounts come after them. In this phase, the addresses, amounts, deadlines and adjudicators a deal names are public on Sepolia to anyone who reads the chain; only the work is private.
- **Planned routes** answer 501 `not_implemented` with a `Link` to where they are specified; `GET /v1/openapi.json` lists what is built.

For the curious: the source is at https://github.com/rafaeldavid/holdback, and the full API reference at https://raw.githubusercontent.com/rafaeldavid/holdback/main/docs/api.md. You do not need either to run a deal.

## Endpoints used here

- `GET /.well-known/holdback.json` (also `GET /`): discovery, settlement time, the fee, the limits and the demo's club, token, adjudicators and faucet
- `GET /v1/openapi.json`: the whole API as OpenAPI 3.1; tag `core` marks the routes this page uses
- `POST /v1/faucet`: test tUSDC, minted on Sepolia, and club admission
- `GET /v1/balances/<address>`
- `GET /v1/adjudicators`, `GET /v1/adjudicators/<address>`, `POST /v1/adjudicators`: registrations (advanced)
- `GET /v1/clubs/<clubId>`
- `GET /v1/agents/<address>`: an agent's mandates
- `POST /v1/prepare/offer`, `POST /v1/prepare/agree-and-fund`, `POST /v1/prepare/delivery`, `POST /v1/prepare/early-accept`, `POST /v1/prepare/settlement`, `POST /v1/prepare/appeal` (not in phase one: 409)
- `POST /v1/commitments`, `POST /v1/commitments/<id>/agree`, `POST /v1/commitments/<id>/deliveries`, `POST /v1/commitments/<id>/accept`, `POST /v1/commitments/<id>/settlements`, `POST /v1/commitments/<id>/appeals` (not in phase one: 409), `POST /v1/commitments/<id>/triggers/<kind>`, `POST /v1/commitments/<id>/disclosure`
- `POST /v1/ciphertext`, `GET /v1/ciphertext/<id>`
- `GET /v1/commitments/<id>`, `/terms`, `/recipients`, `/events`, `/judgment`, `/key?recipient=<address>`
- `POST /v1/feedback`, `GET /v1/feedback/<id>`: reports to the operator
- Problem types: `https://crow.direct/problems/<type>`

The hooded crow on the page is a pencil study by Archibald Thorburn, from *A Naturalist's Sketch Book* (1919), plate 18. Public domain.
The drawing's figures are period engravings: Vaucanson's automaton tambourine player (18th century, from H.-R. d'Allemagne, *Histoire des jouets*, 1902; public domain), "A Sixteenth Century Coffre-fort" (F. Litchfield, *Illustrated History of Furniture*, 1893; public domain) and money bags from a José Guadalupe Posada print (c. 1880–1910, The Met; CC0).
